messages:
mina: Heads-up: ran into a logging/redaction mismatch in the node and python quickstarts. Debug logs from underlying servers (nodemon/uvicorn) are showing request IDs or tokens before our redaction filter runs.

luke: ugh. Minimal repro?

mina: For node quickstart: start with LOG_LEVEL=debug + nodemon --watch. The access logs include request_id in DEBUG lines, but our app-level middleware redacts at INFO. Example: 
```
[DEBUG] nodemon: restarting child - reqid=tmp-777
[DEBUG] express: parsed auth - reqid=tmp-777
[INFO] app.handler: user.login - reqid=REDACTED
```
If I flip init order to register telemetry redaction earlier it fixes, but nodemon/reload spawns child processes with different handler order and it becomes flaky.

anya: same pattern we saw with uvicorn. The root cause is some external loggers creating handlers or emitting logs before our redaction filter is attached to them. In reload modes the server process can add handlers before app startup runs.

luke: two angles: (1) make the SDK provide a robust register_redaction_for_common_servers() helper that is idempotent and attaches filters to uvicorn.access, gunicorn.access, nodemon, pm2 loggers; (2) improve quickstarts to call telemetry.init() as early as possible and document caveats for --reload/dev modes.

mina: I prototyped a tiny helper in the node SDK that iterates over ['nodemon','pm2','express','http','pino'] and calls logger.addFilter(redactionFilter) if available. It seems to cover most leaks.

anya: nice. For python, a similar helper should attach the filter to 'uvicorn.access' and 'gunicorn.access' and also configure structlog so the filter is applied before handlers are created. Maybe expose register_known_logger_filters() on telemetry.init() options.

luke: agree. Also add quickstart CI tests: start the dev server programmatically in a subprocess with LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG, emit a request with a fake token, and assert no unredacted token/reqid appears in logs. Keep tests flaky-proof by retrying startup and using temp files for logs.

ci-bot: CI job queued for PR draft #401 - running quickstart smoke tests.

telemetry-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/1610 - "Dev quickstarts: server dev/reload mode can bypass redaction; add SDK helper + onboarding notes" Labels: devex, telemetry, bug.

mina: I'll push a small PR to node and python quickstarts with the helper and a one-liner in the README about init order. I'll link the CI smoke test.

anya: also add a short note in telemetry docs explaining why dev reload modes can be leaky and recommend running the helper or disabling auto-reload when verifying redaction.

luke: thanks. If we make the helper default-enabled on telemetry.init() (opt-out via env var), we might prevent most user hits. But let's be conservative and keep it opt-in with strong docs for now.

mina: PR incoming in a few hours, will ping here for review.
